_comment: This is the tier that must keep working when the web shell does not.
The shell is fetched over the network; if it 404s, throws, or hangs,
anything it owned dies with it. Bindings defined here still work in
that state, which is the difference between a broken desktop UI and a
machine you cannot quit without switching to a TTY.
The shell may add more bindings at runtime with bind.add over IPC.
That layer is additive and expendable; keep exit and a terminal here.
Precedence: command-line flags > this file > built-in defaults.
Defining any "binds" object at all suppresses the built-in defaults,
so an empty one means 'no keybindings'.
_layout: "tiling"   i3/sway: splits, plus tabbed and stacked containers.
"scrolling" niri: an endless strip of columns that scrolls to follow
focus. Opening a window never resizes the ones already
open. Changes the default movement bindings to match:
Mod4+h/l walk the strip, Mod4+j/k move inside a column,
